paper.title: Incentive-Aware Recommender Systems in Two-Sided Markets

unmapped: myopic agents follow the recommendation only if E[X_{I_t}|I_t, E_t] >= c_* (incentive constraint); the designer controls the information message E_t
homogeneous opportunity cost c_* is known to the designer
the mean reward of arm 1 is known and mu_1 > c_*
the designer uses the probabilities P(mu_i - c_* >= tau) (prior-type quantity) to set theta_tau
settings.definition_quote: When an agent $t$ pulls an arm $i\in\AA$, the agent receives a stochastic reward $X_{i,t}$ that is drawn i.i.d.\ from $[0,1]$ with mean $\mu_{i}$. ... Agent $t$ chooses $y_t=1$ if and only if Eq.~(1) holds. ... Assume that arm $i=1$'s expected reward is known and greater than the cost, $\mu_1>c_*$.

unmapped: agents with private heterogeneous opportunity costs decide whether to follow the recommendation (y_t in {0,1}); bounds hold for any action sequence y_t
loss l(I_t,y_t) = max_i E[X_i - X_{I_t} y_t] depends on agent action; stochastic rewards in [0,1] combined with arbitrary agent action sequence
settings.definition_quote: Each agent's opportunity cost can be \emph{private}, heterogenous, and unknown to the designer. ... for any arm set $\AA$ and action sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$

symbols.L_ARP: L^* = L_1+...+L_m, total number of rounds in Step 2 (sampling) of ARP

conditions: opportunity costs homogeneous c_t = c_* known to designer
tuning: k >= max{9/(2 lambda^2) ln(20m/lambda), theta_tau^2 ln(T theta_tau)}

source.label: lem:regretofknowncost
source.quote: Suppose the assumption in Eq.~\eqref{eqn:positiveplat} holds, and the parameters $\lambda,\theta_\tau, k$ are chosen by ... Let $\gamma_t=1$ in Eq.~\eqref{eqn:egofht}. Then the ARP procedure in Algorithm 1 achieves ex-post regret, $R_T \leq L^*+O\left(\sqrt{mT\ln(mT)}\right)$, where $L^* \equiv L_1+\cdots+L_m$ is the total number of rounds in Step 2 of ARP

results.notes: Paper's m is K. L* lies outside the O(.) in the paper and is itself random. The regret type is ambiguous ('ex-post regret' built from expected per-round losses), so it is recorded as regret_unspecified.

conditions: holds for any action sequence y_t

source.label: thm:regretexpweight
source.quote: If the parameters $\eta=\sqrt{(8\ln m)/T}$ and $\gamma_t\equiv 1$ in Eq.~\eqref{eqn:egofht}, then for any arm set $\AA$ and action sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$, the MARP procedure in Algorithm 2 satisfies, with probability at least $1-\delta$ for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, $R_T\leq \sqrt{\frac{T}{2}\ln m} +  \sqrt{\frac{T}{2}\ln\frac{1}{\delta}}$

results.notes: Paper's m is K. Mapping the environment is uncertain because rewards are stochastic but the agent action sequence is arbitrary.

conditions: minimax over arm sets of size m and action sequences y_t

source.label: thm:lowerbd
source.quote: For any arm set $\AA$ and action sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$, the minimax regret $R^\dagger_T$ satisfies $\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{R^\dagger_T }{(1-\epsilon_T)\sqrt{T\ln m/2}}=1$

results.notes: Stated as an asymptotic equality; the proof only establishes the lower-bound direction. The hard instance has mu_i in {0,1} with random agent actions.

conditions: holds for any action sequence y_t

source.label: thm:nearoptimaldivergingT
source.quote: If the parameter $\eta$ is chosen as $\eta_t=\sqrt{(8\ln m)/t}$ for $t\geq 1$, then for any arm set $\AA$ and action sequence $\{y_t\}_{t=1}^T\in\YY^T$, the MARP procedure in Algorithm 2 satisfies, with probability at least $1-\delta$ for any $\delta\in(0,1)$, $R_T\leq \sqrt{2T\ln m} +\sqrt{\frac{\ln m}{8}} +  \sqrt{\frac{T}{2}\ln\frac{1}{\delta}}$

results.notes: This is the anytime variant with a time-varying learning rate, so T is not needed. Paper's m is K.
